passages.subject: psychology / procrastination
passages.text: Most people think of procrastination as a problem of time management, but researchers increasingly see it as a problem of emotion. When a task feels boring, difficult or uncertain, it triggers an unpleasant mood. Putting the task off removes that mood at once, so the delay is rewarded immediately. The cost arrives later, and the brain gives far less weight to costs that lie in the future. This explains a common paradox. People who procrastinate are not usually lazy, and many of them work hard on other things while the important task waits. In fact, they often perceive the delayed task as more significant than the rest of their work. Its importance is exactly what makes it threatening. For this reason, simple advice to plan better tends to fail. It treats the symptom rather than the underlying cause, and a detailed timetable does nothing to alleviate the anxiety that the task provokes. Studies suggest that smaller steps are more effective. Researchers describe this as a form of emotional regulation, and it can be learned like any other skill. Making the first action very easy lowers the emotional threshold for starting. Forgiving oneself after a delay also helps, because guilt about past procrastination tends to reinforce the next delay. None of this means that deadlines are useless. External deadlines remain one of the most robust tools against delay. However, they work by changing the reward rather than the habit, and the habit usually returns once the deadline has passed.

passages.subject: tourism / overcrowded historic cities
passages.text: In several historic cities, residents now complain that tourism has become a burden rather than a benefit. The problem is not tourism itself but its concentration. Visitors tend to arrive in the same months, stay in the same few streets and photograph the same buildings. As a result, a small area absorbs a disproportionate share of the pressure. Short-term rental platforms have exacerbated the situation. When an apartment earns more from visitors than from a long-term tenant, owners have a strong incentive to switch. Rents rise and local shops are replaced by souvenir stores. The residents who gave the place its character gradually move out, and this slowly erodes the very atmosphere that attracted visitors in the first place. Some cities have tried to curb the flow with entry fees or daily limits. Others have imposed restrictions on new hotels and rental licences. The results are mixed. The measures are difficult to enforce, and tourism remains an indispensable source of income for many families. Critics argue that fees mainly deter poorer visitors while wealthy tourists continue to come. Supporters reply that some form of control is necessary if the centre is to remain a viable neighbourhood and not an open-air museum. Most experts agree on one point. The issue cannot be solved by the tourism sector alone. Housing, transport and planning all play a role, and a solution in one area may simply divert the problem to another.

passages.subject: linguistics / English as a shared language
passages.text: When people from different countries communicate in English, the native speakers in the room are not always the easiest to understand. This finding contradicts a prevalent belief, but it is consistent with a growing body of research. Non-native speakers who share English as a second language tend to adapt their speech. They speak at a steady pace, avoid idioms and make their meaning explicit. Native speakers, by contrast, often assume that their own way of speaking is the standard. They use local expressions, speak quickly and rarely adjust their language to the audience. In international meetings, this can inadvertently exclude the very people they are trying to persuade. Some companies now offer training to native speakers on how to communicate in global English. The notion that native speakers need lessons in their own language may seem strange. However, the skill being taught is not grammar but awareness. Several international firms report that their meetings run more smoothly after such training. The training encourages speakers to notice subtle signs that a listener is not following and to rephrase when necessary. The underlying assumption is that clarity is a shared responsibility. For non-native speakers, the research offers some reassurance. A strong accent rarely hinders communication as much as people fear. What matters more is the willingness of both sides to check and negotiate meaning. This is a skill that is acquired through practice, and there is no compelling evidence that it is innate.

passages.subject: cultural economics / music streaming
passages.text: Streaming has made almost all recorded music available for a monthly fee, yet many musicians say they earn less than before. The explanation lies in how the money is divided. Most platforms collect subscription fees into a single pool and then share it according to each artist's proportion of total plays. Under this model, a listener who plays only a few jazz albums still contributes to the income of the most popular pop stars. Critics argue that the system therefore favours artists who already have huge audiences. An alternative, known as the user-centric model, would allocate each subscriber's fee only to the artists that this person actually listens to. Proponents claim that it would be fairer and would reward loyal fans. However, studies of this model have produced tentative and sometimes surprising results. In several simulations, the change shifted only a marginal amount of money, and some smaller artists actually received less. The reason is that heavy users, who play music for many hours a day, tend to listen to mainstream songs. Under the current model, their fees partly subsidise the artists that lighter users enjoy. As long as the pool remains small, the debate about how to divide it is likely to persist. A further problem is scale. Even a fair division of a small pool cannot sustain a career if the pool itself is too small. For this reason, there is a substantial discrepancy between what musicians earn from recordings and what they earn on stage, and many now depend on live performances.

passages.subject: ethics / modern zoos
passages.text: Modern zoos present themselves as centres of conservation rather than places of entertainment. Many of them run breeding programmes for vulnerable species and fund research in the wild. Some animals, including certain antelopes and birds, survive today largely because zoos maintained viable populations when wild numbers collapsed. For their supporters, this record provides a compelling argument for their existence. Critics, however, point out that only a small proportion of zoo animals belong to threatened species. Large and popular animals such as elephants and polar bears attract visitors but rarely benefit from captivity. These animals often show signs of stress that persist despite improvements in their enclosures. Better enclosures can mitigate some of this stress, but they cannot remove it. Critics also question the educational claims that zoos make. Visitors typically spend less than a minute at each enclosure, which hardly constitutes a lesson in ecology. Zoos reply that even a brief visit can foster a lasting interest in nature, especially among children. In addition, some zoos now return animals to protected areas in the wild when conditions allow it. The debate is unlikely to be settled by evidence alone, because it also involves values. One side asks whether keeping animals in captivity can ever be legitimate. The other asks whether the alternative would be any better in a world where habitats are disappearing. A growing number of zoos have responded by keeping fewer large mammals and more of the animals that conservation programmes can genuinely help.

questions.subject: citizen science / volunteer bird counts
questions.stem: Although the volunteers who count the birds in their gardens every winter have no scientific training, ----.

options.o1: their combined records have proved robust enough to reveal long-term trends in bird numbers
options.o2: their combined records are too unreliable to be used by any professional researcher
options.o3: the counting takes place over a single weekend in the coldest part of the year
options.o4: most of them begin by learning to recognise the birds that visit their feeders
options.o5: the organisers send every participant a simple form and a guide to common species

questions.why: Although bir ödün bağlacıdır: eğitimsiz gönüllülere rağmen kayıtların işe yaradığı söylenmelidir. robust burada 'sağlam, güvenilir' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Eğitimsizlikten beklenen sonucu tekrarlar; Although'ın istediği karşıtlık kurulmaz.

questions.subject: recruitment / the job interview
questions.stem: Research on hiring suggests that informal interviews without a fixed list of questions are a poor guide to future performance, because ----.

options.o1: interviewers tend to favour candidates who resemble them, which can distort their judgement
options.o2: every candidate is asked exactly the same questions in exactly the same order
options.o3: most companies now ask applicants to complete an online test before the interview
options.o4: the interview is often the first time that a candidate visits the company's offices
options.o5: employers are required by law to keep a written record of every question they ask

questions.why: because bir neden ister: sabit soru listesi olmayınca görüşmeci kendine benzeyeni kayırır ve yargısı çarpılır. distort 'çarpıtmak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Bu seçenek sabit soru listeli, yani yapılandırılmış görüşmeyi tarif eder; köktekinin tam tersidir.

questions.subject: health services / hospital volunteers
questions.stem: Hospitals that rely on volunteers to guide visitors and serve tea in the waiting areas find that the arrangement works well ----.

options.o1: as long as the volunteers' tasks are confined to areas that do not overlap with the work of paid staff
options.o2: only when the volunteers are given the same duties as the nurses on the wards
options.o3: because most visitors are unable to find their way around a large building
options.o4: although many volunteers are retired people who live close to the hospital
options.o5: so that patients can receive their medicine at the correct time every day

questions.why: as long as bir koşul bildirir: düzen, gönüllülerin işi ücretli personelin işiyle çakışmadıkça yürür. confine 'sınırlamak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Koşulu tersine çevirir: gönüllülere hemşire görevi vermek düzeni bozar, işletmez.

questions.subject: media / online restaurant reviews
questions.stem: Since a restaurant with hundreds of reviews is unlikely to be harmed by one unfair comment from an angry customer, ----.

options.o1: the owners of small and new restaurants are the most vulnerable to a single hostile review
options.o2: the owners of large and popular restaurants are the most vulnerable to a single hostile review
options.o3: many diners read the reviews only after they have already booked a table
options.o4: review sites remove comments that contain offensive or personal language
options.o5: restaurants with outdoor seating tend to receive higher ratings in summer

questions.why: Çok yorumu olan restoran tek yorumdan etkilenmiyorsa, en korunmasız olan az yorumu olan küçük ve yeni restorandır. vulnerable 'savunmasız, zarar görmeye açık' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Öncülün sonucunu tersine çevirir; çok sayıda yorum büyük restoranı tam da korunaklı kılar.

questions.subject: technology / noise-cancelling headphones
questions.stem: Noise-cancelling headphones allow commuters to read or work in peace on a crowded train, but in the street they may also ----.

options.o1: impair the user's awareness of announcements or of a cyclist approaching from behind
options.o2: improve the user's awareness of announcements and of a cyclist approaching from behind
options.o3: be sold at a much lower price in the months after a new model appears
options.o4: need to be charged every evening if they are used for several hours a day
options.o5: come with a small hard case that protects them when they are not in use

questions.why: but bir karşıtlık bildirir: trendeki yararın ardından sokaktaki bir sakınca gelmelidir. impair 'zayıflatmak, bozmak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: impair ile improve'u karıştıran okur için hazırlanmıştır; but'ın istediği sakınca yerine bir yarar sayar.

questions.subject: education / homework clubs in libraries
questions.stem: Libraries that run homework clubs after school report that the children who attend most regularly are often those who ----.

options.o1: are deprived of a quiet place to study in their own homes
options.o2: already have a private room for studying in their own homes
options.o3: were asked by their teachers to keep a weekly reading diary
options.o4: usually travel by bus from schools on the other side of town
options.o5: prefer to borrow novels rather than reference books from the shelves

questions.why: Ödev kulübüne en çok, evde çalışacak sessiz yeri olmayan çocuk muhtaçtır. be deprived of 'bir şeyden yoksun olmak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Mantığı tersine çevirir; evde çalışma odası olan çocuk kütüphaneye en az ihtiyaç duyandır.

questions.subject: public health / calorie labels on menus
questions.stem: Although restaurants were required by law to print the number of calories next to every dish on the menu, ----.

options.o1: the effect on what most customers actually ordered turned out to be negligible
options.o2: most customers immediately began to choose the lightest dishes on the menu
options.o3: because customers had been asking for this information for many years
options.o4: so diners were able to compare the prices of similar dishes more easily
options.o5: the figures were printed in the same colour as the prices of the dishes

questions.why: Although bir karşıtlık ister: yasal zorunluluğa rağmen etki önemsiz kalmıştır. negligible 'yok denecek kadar az' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Yasanın beklenen sonucunu söyler; ödün bağlacından sonra beklenen değil, beklenmeyen gelir.

questions.subject: urban life / allotment gardens
questions.stem: In many cities the waiting lists for the small plots of land that residents rent to grow vegetables have grown so long that ----.

options.o1: some applicants wait for more than a decade before they are allocated a plot
options.o2: most applicants are allocated a plot within a few weeks of applying for one
options.o3: the gardens are usually located close to railway lines or to rivers
options.o4: the tradition of growing vegetables in towns goes back two centuries
options.o5: the soil in the older plots often contains a great deal of heavy clay

questions.why: so ... that yapısı bir sonuç bildirir: liste o kadar uzundur ki bazı başvuranlar on yıldan fazla bekler. allocate 'tahsis etmek' demektir.
questions.trap_note: so long that ile çelişir: liste uzunsa yer birkaç haftada çıkmaz.

questions.subject: consumer behaviour / unused gym memberships
questions.stem: Gyms are able to keep their monthly fees surprisingly low, partly because a large proportion of their members ----.

options.o1: persist in paying for facilities that they hardly ever use
options.o2: use the facilities every day and bring their friends along
options.o3: live within walking distance of the nearest branch of the gym
options.o4: prefer to exercise in the early morning or late in the evening
options.o5: receive a free personal training session when they first join

questions.why: Düşük ücretin nedeni, parası ödenip kullanılmayan kapasitedir. persist in doing 'yapmayı sürdürmek' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Herkes her gün gelseydi salon kalabalıklaşır ve ücret düşük tutulamazdı; seçenek nedeni tersine çevirir.

questions.subject: broadcasting / sign-language interpreters
questions.stem: Many deaf viewers prefer to see a sign-language interpreter on the screen rather than read subtitles, because a signed translation ----.

options.o1: conveys tone and emphasis that written subtitles cannot easily render
options.o2: is a word-for-word copy of the spoken language that subtitles show
options.o3: is taught in most primary schools as an optional subject
options.o4: was first used on national television several decades ago
options.o5: requires the interpreter to work in a well-lit studio

questions.why: because bir neden ister: işaret dili, altyazının aktaramadığı tonu ve vurguyu taşır. render burada 'aktarmak, yansıtmak' anlamındadır.
questions.trap_note: İşaret dilini konuşmanın birebir kopyası sayar; öyle olsaydı altyazıya bir üstünlüğü kalmazdı.

questions.subject: museums / audio guides
questions.stem: Audio guides allow visitors to explore a museum at their own pace, but they can also inhibit conversation between people who came together.

options.o1: Sesli rehberler ziyaretçilerin müzeyi kendi hızlarında gezmelerini sağlar, ancak birlikte gelen insanlar arasındaki sohbeti de engelleyebilir.
options.o2: Sesli rehberler birlikte gelen insanların sohbet etmesini kolaylaştırır, ancak ziyaretçilerin müzeyi kendi hızlarında gezmesini engelleyebilir.
options.o3: Birlikte gelen ziyaretçiler, sohbet edebilmek için sesli rehber kullanmamayı tercih etmektedir.
options.o4: Sesli rehberler, ziyaretçilerin müzede daha uzun süre kalmasına yol açmaktadır.
options.o5: Müzeler, ziyaretçiler arasındaki sohbeti azaltmak amacıyla sesli rehber sunmaktadır.

questions.why: Cümlenin iki yarısı but ile bağlanır: önce bir yarar, sonra bir sakınca. inhibit 'engellemek, bastırmak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Yarar ile sakıncayı yer değiştirir; aynı sözcüklerle cümlenin tersi kurulur.

questions.subject: transport / car-sharing schemes
questions.stem: Car-sharing schemes are most viable in dense neighbourhoods where few residents need a car every day.

options.o1: Araç paylaşım sistemleri, pek az sakinin her gün arabaya ihtiyaç duyduğu yoğun mahallelerde en çok uygulanabilir.
options.o2: Araç paylaşım sistemleri, sakinlerin çoğunun her gün arabaya ihtiyaç duyduğu seyrek mahallelerde en çok uygulanabilir.
options.o3: Yoğun mahallelerde yaşayanlar araç paylaşım sistemlerini her gün kullanmaktadır.
options.o4: Araç paylaşım sistemleri yoğun mahallelerde araba sahipliğini tamamen ortadan kaldırmıştır.
options.o5: Sakinlerin az olduğu mahallelerde araç paylaşımına neredeyse hiç ihtiyaç duyulmaz.

questions.why: viable 'uygulanabilir, ayakta kalabilir' demektir; koşul yoğun mahalle ve arabaya az ihtiyaçtır.
questions.trap_note: few'u 'çoğu' diye okur ve mahalleyi de seyrekleştirir; iki koşul birden tersine döner.

questions.subject: language learning / app streaks
questions.stem: Daily streaks keep learners coming back to a language app, but they may inadvertently reward the habit of opening the app rather than the effort of learning.

options.o1: Günlük seriler öğrencilerin bir dil uygulamasına geri dönmesini sağlar, ancak farkında olmadan öğrenme çabasını değil, uygulamayı açma alışkanlığını ödüllendiriyor olabilir.
options.o2: Günlük seriler öğrencilerin bir dil uygulamasına geri dönmesini sağlar, ancak farkında olmadan uygulamayı açma alışkanlığını değil, öğrenme çabasını ödüllendiriyor olabilir.
options.o3: Günlük seriler, öğrencilerin uygulamayı her gün açmasını zorunlu kılan bir kuraldır.
options.o4: Dil uygulamaları öğrenme çabasını ödüllendirmek için günlük seriler geliştirmiştir.
options.o5: Uygulamayı her gün açan öğrenciler dili daha hızlı öğrenmektedir.

questions.why: rather than kalıbında ödüllendirilen ilk ögedir: açma alışkanlığı. inadvertently 'farkında olmadan, istemeden' demektir.
questions.trap_note: rather than'in iki ucunu değiştirir; cümle bu kez bir övgüye döner.

questions.subject: workplace / open-plan offices
questions.stem: Açık ofisler iş birliğini kolaylaştırmak için tasarlanmıştır, ancak birçok çalışan dikkatinin dağılmaması için kulaklık takmaktadır.

options.o1: Open-plan offices were designed to facilitate collaboration, but many employees wear headphones so that they are not distracted.
options.o2: Open-plan offices were designed to reduce collaboration, so many employees wear headphones in order to share their ideas.
options.o3: Employees in open-plan offices wear headphones because collaboration is not allowed there.
options.o4: Open-plan offices were designed for employees who prefer to work with headphones on.
options.o5: Many employees asked for open-plan offices so that they could collaborate more easily.

questions.why: 'kolaylaştırmak' facilitate ile karşılanır; ancak ile kurulan karşıtlık da but ile korunmalıdır.
questions.trap_note: facilitate yerine reduce koyar ve karşıtlığı bir sonuç ilişkisine çevirir.

questions.subject: law / jury service
questions.stem: Jüri görevine çağrılan kişilerin bir kısmı, işlerini kaybetme korkusuyla muafiyet talep etmektedir.

options.o1: Some of the people who are summoned for jury service ask to be exempted because they fear losing their jobs.
options.o2: Some of the people who are exempted from jury service fear that they will lose their jobs as a result.
options.o3: People who are afraid of losing their jobs are never summoned for jury service.
options.o4: Most of the people summoned for jury service are exempted by their employers.
options.o5: Jury service is compulsory only for people who are not in employment.

questions.why: Cümlede sıra şöyledir: çağrılırlar, iş kaybı korkusuyla muafiyet isterler. exempt 'muaf tutmak' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Muafiyeti olmuş bir şey sayar ve korkuyu onun sonucu yapar; neden ile sonuç yer değiştirir.

questions.subject: environmental policy / plastic bag charges
questions.stem: Plastik poşetler için alınan küçük bir ücret bile tam bir yasaktan daha kolay uygulanır ve tüketim üzerinde şaşırtıcı derecede güçlü bir etki yaratır.

options.o1: Even a small charge for plastic bags is easier to implement than a complete ban and has a surprisingly profound effect on consumption.
options.o2: A complete ban on plastic bags is easier to implement than a small charge and has a surprisingly profound effect on consumption.
options.o3: A small charge for plastic bags affects consumption only when it is combined with a ban.
options.o4: Consumers who pay a small charge for plastic bags tend to use them more often.
options.o5: A complete ban on plastic bags has now been implemented in most countries.

questions.why: Karşılaştırmanın kazananı küçük ücrettir: daha kolay uygulanır ve etkisi güçlüdür. profound 'derin, güçlü' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Karşılaştırmanın iki ucunu değiştirir; yasak ile ücret yer değişince cümlenin savı tersine döner.

questions.stem: According to the passage, putting a task off makes people feel better at first because ----.

options.o1: it removes the unpleasant mood that the task produces
options.o2: it gives them more time to manage the task properly
options.o3: it allows them to finish all their other work first
options.o4: the cost of the delay has to be paid immediately
options.o5: other people usually forgive them for the delay

questions.why: Metin açıkça yazar: ertelemek, işin yarattığı tatsız duyguyu hemen ortadan kaldırır, bu yüzden gecikme anında ödüllendirilir.
questions.trap_note: İlk cümledeki 'time management' sözcüklerini tekrar eder; oysa metin ertelemeyi zaman yönetimi sorunu olarak görmeyi reddeder.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that people who procrastinate ----.

options.o1: often regard the task they avoid as especially important
options.o2: are usually too lazy to work hard on anything at all
options.o3: rarely have any other work to do while they wait
options.o4: plan their time more carefully than other people do
options.o5: do not realise that the task will have to be done

questions.why: Metin: 'they often perceive the delayed task as more significant than the rest of their work.' perceive 'algılamak' demektir; seçenek bunu regard ile karşılar.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'genellikle tembel değiller' cümlesiyle doğrudan çelişir; hızlı okuyan 'lazy' sözcüğünü görür, olumsuzluğu kaçırır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a detailed timetable fails to stop procrastination because ----.

options.o1: it does nothing about the feeling that makes the task hard to start
options.o2: it makes the task seem less important than it really is
options.o3: most people cannot follow a timetable for more than a day
options.o4: it removes the external deadline that would otherwise apply
options.o5: it increases the guilt that people feel about past delays

questions.why: Metin: plan 'does nothing to alleviate the anxiety that the task provokes'. alleviate 'hafifletmek', provoke 'yol açmak' demektir; plan duyguya dokunmaz.
questions.trap_note: Metinde olmayan bir mekanizma uydurur; plan önemi azalttığı için değil, kaygıya dokunmadığı için işe yaramaz.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Procrastination is driven by emotion, so the remedies that work best are those that make starting feel less threatening.
options.o2: Procrastination can be cured completely by setting strict external deadlines.
options.o3: People who procrastinate are generally less hard-working than others.
options.o4: Time management courses are the most effective way of ending delay.
options.o5: Guilt is the main reason why people delay their important tasks.

questions.why: Metin ertelemeyi bir duygu sorunu olarak tanımlar ve işe yarayan adımları buna göre sayar: çok küçük bir ilk adım ve kendini affetmek.
questions.trap_note: Son cümleyi atlar: teslim tarihleri işe yarar ama alışkanlığı değiştirmez; tarih geçince alışkanlık geri döner.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the main problem with tourism in historic cities is ----.

options.o1: that visitors crowd into a few places at the same times of year
options.o2: that the total number of tourists has become too large for any city
options.o3: that tourists spend too little money in the local shops
options.o4: that historic buildings are damaged by constant photography
options.o5: that residents refuse to rent their apartments to visitors

questions.why: Metin açıkça ayırır: sorun turizmin kendisi değil, yoğunlaşmasıdır; ziyaretçiler aynı aylarda aynı birkaç sokağa gelir.
questions.trap_note: Metnin ayırdığı iki şeyi birleştirir: sorun toplam ziyaretçi sayısı değil, ziyaretçilerin nerede ve ne zaman toplandığıdır.

questions.stem: According to the passage, short-term rental platforms have made the situation worse because ----.

options.o1: owners can earn more from visitors than from long-term tenants
options.o2: visitors who use them stay much longer than hotel guests
options.o3: they have replaced the souvenir shops in the historic centre
options.o4: the cities concerned have refused to regulate them at all
options.o5: residents use them to rent rooms to their own relatives

questions.why: Soru kökündeki 'made the situation worse', metindeki 'exacerbated the situation' ifadesinin karşılığıdır. Hemen ardından gelen cümle nedeni verir: daire turistten daha çok kazandırınca sahiplerin güçlü bir teşviki (incentive) olur.
questions.trap_note: Metinde hiç geçmeyen bir bilgiyi neden yapar; sorun kalış süresi değil, kira gelirindeki farktır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that entry fees for visitors ----.

options.o1: may change who visits a city more than how many people visit it
options.o2: have succeeded in reducing the number of visitors in every city
options.o3: are the only measure that cities have tried so far
options.o4: are welcomed by the families who depend on tourism
options.o5: were introduced mainly to pay for new hotels

questions.why: Eleştirmenlere göre ücret daha çok yoksul ziyaretçiyi caydırır, varlıklılar gelmeye devam eder; yani ücret sayıdan çok ziyaretçinin kim olduğunu değiştirir.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'sonuçlar karışık' yargısını görmezden gelir ve 'her kentte' diyerek aşırı bir genelleme yapar.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Tourism harms historic cities mainly when it is concentrated, and no single policy can solve the problem on its own.
options.o2: Historic cities should ban short-term rentals in order to protect their residents.
options.o3: Tourists should be encouraged to visit historic cities in the winter months.
options.o4: Entry fees are the most effective way of controlling tourism.
options.o5: Historic cities depend on tourism more than on any other industry.

questions.why: Metin sorunu yoğunlaşmaya bağlar, önlemlerin karışık sonuç verdiğini söyler ve tek bir sektörün çözemeyeceğiyle bitirir.
questions.trap_note: Metnin vermediği bir öneriyi ana fikir yapar; kiralama platformları sorunun bir parçası olarak anılır, yasak önerilmez.

questions.stem: According to the passage, non-native speakers who use English with one another ----.

options.o1: avoid idioms and make their meaning explicit
options.o2: speak more quickly than native speakers usually do
options.o3: rarely check whether they have been understood
options.o4: prefer to use local expressions in meetings
options.o5: find native speakers easier to follow than other learners

questions.why: Metin sayar: sabit bir hızla konuşur, deyimlerden kaçınır ve anlamlarını açık seçik (explicit) kılarlar.
questions.trap_note: Ana dili konuşanlara ait bir özelliği yabancılara yükler; metinde hızlı konuşan taraf ana dili konuşanlardır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that native speakers who receive training in global English ----.

options.o1: learn to notice when a listener has lost track of what they are saying
options.o2: are taught the grammar of their own language all over again
options.o3: are advised to stop using English in international meetings
options.o4: are expected to lose their native accent completely
options.o5: usually become less persuasive than they were before

questions.why: Eğitim, dinleyicinin takip edemediğine dair ince (subtle) işaretleri fark etmeyi ve gerekince yeniden ifade etmeyi öğretir.
questions.trap_note: Metnin açıkça reddettiği şeyi söyler: öğretilen beceri dilbilgisi değil, farkındalıktır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that a strong foreign accent ----.

options.o1: causes fewer problems in communication than people often expect
options.o2: is the main obstacle to communication in international meetings
options.o3: is regarded as a sign of poor education by most native speakers
options.o4: can be removed through the training described in the passage
options.o5: makes speakers more careful about checking meaning

questions.why: Metin: 'A strong accent rarely hinders communication as much as people fear.' hinder 'engellemek' demektir; aksan sanıldığı kadar engel olmaz.
questions.trap_note: rarely sözcüğünü atlayan okur cümleyi tersine anlar; metin aksanı ana engel saymaz.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Clear international communication depends less on being a native speaker than on both sides adjusting to each other.
options.o2: Native speakers of English communicate worse than non-native speakers in every situation.
options.o3: Companies should stop hiring native speakers for international roles.
options.o4: Learning idioms is the most important step in mastering English.
options.o5: A strong accent is the main reason why international meetings fail.

questions.why: Metin açıklığın ortak bir sorumluluk olduğunu söyler ve iki tarafın anlamı birlikte kurma isteğini belirleyici sayar.
questions.trap_note: Metnin 'not always' dediği yerde 'her durumda' der; dikkatli bir saptamayı aşırı bir genellemeye çevirir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that under the current model, a listener who plays only jazz ----.

options.o1: still helps to pay the most popular pop stars
options.o2: pays only for the jazz albums that he actually plays
options.o3: pays a lower monthly fee than a pop listener does
options.o4: is left out of the platform's single pool of fees
options.o5: receives a small share of the income himself

questions.why: Metin bunu örnekle verir: yalnızca caz dinleyen bir kullanıcı bile en popüler pop yıldızlarının gelirine katkıda bulunur.
questions.trap_note: Bu, metinde 'alternatif' olarak anlatılan kullanıcı merkezli modeldir; şimdiki modeli değil, önerilen modeli tarif eder.

questions.stem: According to the passage, studies of the user-centric model found that ----.

options.o1: the change moved very little money and sometimes hurt smaller artists
options.o2: the change transferred a large amount of money to smaller artists
options.o3: heavy users would stop paying for their subscriptions
options.o4: listeners preferred the system that pools all the fees
options.o5: the model was impossible to calculate in practice

questions.why: Metin: 'the change shifted only a marginal amount of money, and some smaller artists actually received less.' marginal 'çok küçük, önemsiz' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Modelin savunucularının beklediği sonucu söyler; metin tam da bu beklentinin gerçekleşmediğini anlatır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that people who listen to music for many hours a day ----.

options.o1: currently help to support the artists that lighter users prefer
options.o2: are the main source of income for jazz musicians
options.o3: pay higher fees than light users on most platforms
options.o4: would gain nothing from either of the two models
options.o5: prefer live performances to recorded music

questions.why: Metin: şimdiki modelde yoğun dinleyicilerin ücretleri hafif dinleyicilerin sevdiği sanatçıları kısmen destekler (subsidise).
questions.trap_note: Yoğun dinleyicileri caza bağlar; metin tam tersine onların ana akım şarkılar dinlediğini söyler.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Dividing streaming money differently would help musicians less than expected, because the size of the total is the deeper problem.
options.o2: The user-centric model would solve the financial problems of most musicians.
options.o3: Pop stars receive far too much money from streaming platforms.
options.o4: Listeners should pay higher monthly fees for streaming services.
options.o5: Live performances have become less profitable since streaming began.

questions.why: Metin önce bölüşüm tartışmasını anlatır, sonra asıl sorunun havuzun küçüklüğü olduğunu söyler.
questions.trap_note: Metnin çürüttüğü beklentiyi ana fikir yapar; araştırmalar modelin parayı pek az kaydırdığını göstermiştir.

questions.stem: According to the passage, critics point out that only a small proportion of zoo animals ----.

options.o1: belong to species that are actually threatened
options.o2: show signs of stress in their enclosures
options.o3: were born in the wild before arriving at the zoo
options.o4: attract the attention of visitors
options.o5: take part in research programmes in the wild

questions.why: Metin eleştirmenlerin saptamasını birebir verir: hayvanların yalnızca küçük bir kısmı tehdit altındaki türlere aittir.
questions.trap_note: Metindeki 'stress' sözcüğünü yanlış yere bağlar; metne göre büyük hayvanlar sık sık stres belirtisi gösterir, azı değil.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that better enclosures for large animals ----.

options.o1: can reduce their stress without removing it
options.o2: have removed all signs of stress in these animals
options.o3: were built mainly in order to attract more visitors
options.o4: are more important than breeding programmes
options.o5: have made zoos more popular with children

questions.why: Metin: 'Better enclosures can mitigate some of this stress, but they cannot remove it.' mitigate 'hafifletmek' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Cümlenin ikinci yarısını, yani 'but they cannot remove it' kısmını okumayan kişinin seçeceği şıktır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the debate about zoos cannot be settled by evidence alone because ----.

options.o1: people disagree about what is acceptable, not only about what is true
options.o2: there is not yet enough evidence about stress in zoo animals
options.o3: zoos refuse to publish the results of their research
options.o4: visitors spend too little time at each enclosure
options.o5: habitats are disappearing faster than zoos can respond

questions.why: Metin gerekçeyi verir: tartışma değerlere de dayanır; bir taraf hayvanı esaret altında tutmanın hiç meşru (legitimate) olup olmadığını sorar.
questions.trap_note: Kökteki 'evidence' sözcüğüne takılır; metin kanıtın eksikliğinden değil, işin içinde değer yargısı olmasından söz eder.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Zoos make a strong case through conservation, but the case applies to some animals far more than to others.
options.o2: Zoos should be closed because they fail to educate their visitors.
options.o3: Breeding programmes are the only reason why zoos still exist.
options.o4: Children learn more about nature from zoos than from any other source.
options.o5: Large mammals such as elephants benefit most from life in a zoo.

questions.why: Metin koruma savını güçlü bulur, büyük hayvanlar için zayıf bulur ve hayvanat bahçelerinin koleksiyonlarını buna göre değiştirdiğini söyler.
questions.trap_note: Eleştirilerden birini kesin bir yargıya çevirir; metin hayvanat bahçelerinin kapatılmasını önermez.

questions.subject: hospitality / laptop workers in cafés
dialogue: Not at first. They buy one coffee and stay for four hours, and a table that turns over six times at lunch only turns over once.
We kept the wifi free but turned off the sockets at the busiest tables. Nobody was asked to leave, and the problem resolved itself within a month.

options.o1: Were you pleased when people began to use your café as an office?
options.o2: Do you charge your customers for using the wifi?
options.o3: How many tables does your café have at the moment?
options.o4: Where did you learn to make such good coffee?
options.o5: Do most of your customers come from the nearby offices?

questions.why: Yanıt 'Önce hayır' der ve dizüstü bilgisayarla saatlerce oturanların yarattığı sorunu anlatır; boşluk kafeyi ofis gibi kullananlardan memnun olup olmadığını sormalıdır.
questions.trap_note: 'Not at first' bu soruya da uyuyor gibi görünür, ama sahip son replikte Wi-Fi'nin ücretsiz kaldığını söyler; ücret hiç konu olmamıştır.

questions.subject: workplace / mentoring schemes
dialogue: Your company pairs every new employee with a mentor from a different department. Why not someone from their own team?
Because a mentor from the same team is also the person who will judge their work. New staff hesitate to admit what they do not understand to someone who will assess them.
Exactly. Someone from outside has nothing to gain or lose from their performance, so the questions come out much more easily.

options.o1: So the distance between them is what makes honesty possible?
options.o2: So the mentor is also responsible for assessing the new employee?
options.o3: How long does the mentoring arrangement usually last?
options.o4: Do the mentors receive any training before they start?
options.o5: Are new employees allowed to choose their own mentor?

questions.why: Yönetici 'Kesinlikle' diye onaylar ve dışarıdan birinin neden daha rahat soru sordurduğunu açıklar; boşluk bu mesafenin dürüstlüğü sağladığını özetlemelidir.
questions.trap_note: Yöneticinin az önce kaçınılması gereken durum diye anlattığı şeyi, yani değerlendiren kişinin rehber olmasını, onaylatmaya çalışır.

questions.subject: environment / tree-planting pledges
dialogue: Your organisation has criticised companies that promise to plant a million trees. Surely planting trees is a good thing?
Planting is the easy part. In several large schemes, most of the young trees were dead within three years, because nobody was paid to look after them.
So the number in the press release tells us very little?

options.o1: It tells us how many trees were planted, not how many survived, and only the second figure matters for the climate.
options.o2: It tells us exactly how much carbon the scheme will remove over the next hundred years.
options.o3: It is usually checked by an independent auditor before it is published.
options.o4: It is far smaller than the number of trees cut down in the same year.
options.o5: It refers only to trees planted in tropical countries.

questions.why: Araştırmacı dikilen ile yaşayan ağaç arasındaki farkı anlatmıştır; yanıt sayının bu yüzden az şey söylediğini doğrulamalıdır.
questions.trap_note: Sunucunun 'çok az şey söylüyor' saptamasıyla çelişir ve sayıya, araştırmacının az önce yıktığı bir kesinlik yükler.

questions.subject: technology / voice assistants
dialogue: People claim they speak to their voice assistant more politely than to their own family. Is that true?
Possibly for children. A child who learns that a device obeys a curt command may carry the habit into conversations with people.

options.o1: Some people do, but most speak to the assistant in short commands without any courtesy at all.
options.o2: Yes, almost everyone thanks the device and apologises when they make a mistake.
options.o3: Voice assistants were first sold in large numbers about ten years ago.
options.o4: Families with young children use voice assistants less than other households.
options.o5: Most voice assistants can now recognise the voices of several different users.

questions.why: Son replik çocuğun kısa ve kaba (curt) komutları öğrenmesinden söz eder; boşluk insanların cihaza nezaketsiz konuştuğunu söylemelidir.
questions.trap_note: Sunucunun iddiasını doğrular; ama o zaman son replikteki 'kaba komut alışkanlığı' endişesinin hiçbir dayanağı kalmaz.

questions.subject: urban culture / street art and permission
dialogue: The city removes some murals within a day and protects others as part of its heritage. How does it decide?
Officially, it depends on whether the owner of the wall gave permission. In practice, a painting that becomes popular before anyone reports it tends to stay.
It is, and we know it. But removing something that thousands of residents photograph every week would provoke far more complaints than leaving it.

options.o1: Isn't that rather arbitrary?
options.o2: So permission is the only thing that really matters?
options.o3: How many murals are painted in the city each year?
options.o4: Do the artists usually sign their work?
options.o5: Who pays for the paint that the artists use?

questions.why: Görevli 'Öyle, biliyoruz' diyerek bir eleştiriyi kabul eder; resmî kural ile uygulama arasındaki fark keyfîlik eleştirisini doğurur. arbitrary 'keyfî' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Görevlinin 'uygulamada' diye düzelttiği resmî kuralı tek ölçüt sayar; 'It is, and we know it' yanıtı bu soruya uymaz.

questions.subject: parenting / children's screen time
questions.stem: Limiting children's screen time may do little good if the time saved is simply filled with another passive activity.

options.o1: If the hours taken away from screens are spent on something equally passive, limiting them may bring little benefit.
options.o2: Limiting children's screen time is beneficial only when it is replaced by another passive activity.
options.o3: Children who spend less time on screens usually become more active as a result.
options.o4: Passive activities do children less harm than time spent in front of a screen.
options.o5: Screen time should be limited only for children who are not active enough.

questions.why: if ile kurulan koşul korunur: kazanılan zaman yine edilgen bir uğraşla doluyorsa sınırlamanın yararı azdır.
questions.trap_note: Koşulu tersine çevirir: edilgen uğraşı yararın şartı yapar.

questions.subject: education / second languages in primary school
questions.stem: Introducing a second language in primary school yields the best results when the teachers are themselves confident speakers of it.

options.o1: A second language taught in primary school works best when the teachers speak it with confidence.
options.o2: Teachers become confident speakers of a second language once they introduce it in primary school.
options.o3: A second language should only be introduced after children have left primary school.
options.o4: Most primary school teachers are confident speakers of at least one other language.
options.o5: The results of teaching a second language depend mainly on the age of the children.

questions.why: yield the best results 'en iyi sonucu vermek' demektir; koşul öğretmenin dili rahat konuşmasıdır.
questions.trap_note: Koşul ile sonucu yer değiştirir: öğretmenin özgüveni sonucun nedeni değil, sonucu olur.

questions.subject: schools / school trips
questions.stem: Schools have cut back on trips not because teachers doubt their value but because the paperwork they entail has grown so heavy.

options.o1: Schools organise fewer trips because of the paperwork involved, not because teachers doubt that trips are useful.
options.o2: Schools organise fewer trips because teachers doubt their value, although the paperwork has become lighter.
options.o3: Teachers think school trips are valuable only when all the paperwork has been completed.
options.o4: The paperwork for school trips was introduced because teachers doubted their value.
options.o5: Schools that organise many trips have found ways to reduce the paperwork.

questions.why: not because A but because B kalıbı gerçek nedeni B'ye verir: evrak yükü. entail 'gerektirmek, beraberinde getirmek' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Cümlenin reddettiği nedeni gerçek neden yapar ve evrak yükünü de tersine çevirir.

questions.subject: charity / marathon fundraising
questions.stem: People who raise money by running a marathon often collect more than they would by simply asking, because the effort makes the request more credible.

options.o1: Because the effort of running makes the appeal more believable, runners often collect more money than a simple request would raise.
options.o2: Because a simple request is more believable than a marathon, runners often collect less money than they expect.
options.o3: Most people who run a marathon for charity do so because they find asking for money difficult.
options.o4: Donors prefer to give money to runners who have completed several marathons before.
options.o5: Asking for donations directly usually raises more money than running a marathon does.

questions.why: credible 'inandırıcı' demektir; harcanan emek isteği daha inandırıcı kılar ve daha çok bağış getirir.
questions.trap_note: İnandırıcılığı yanlış tarafa verir ve sonucu da tersine çevirir.

questions.subject: recycling / disposable coffee cups
questions.stem: ---- The cup looks like paper, but the inside is lined with a thin layer of plastic that stops the drink from soaking through. Separating the two materials requires special equipment, and only a handful of plants in the country have it. As a result, most cups that are placed in a recycling bin end up being burned or buried together with ordinary waste.

options.o1: Most disposable coffee cups cannot be recycled in the way their customers assume.
options.o2: Paper coffee cups are now accepted by every recycling plant in the country.
options.o3: Coffee shops have become far more common in city centres over the last twenty years.
options.o4: Some customers bring their own cups and receive a small discount in return.
options.o5: The plastic used in the cups is made from oil and is very cheap to produce.

questions.why: Boşluk paragrafın ilk cümlesidir ve konuyu kurmalıdır; devamı bardağın neden geri dönüştürülemediğini adım adım açıklar.
questions.trap_note: 'Recycling' ve 'paper' sözcükleriyle konuya uyuyor gibi görünür, ama paragrafın 'yalnızca birkaç tesiste' saptamasıyla doğrudan çelişir.

questions.subject: aviation business / frequent-flyer points
questions.stem: Frequent-flyer schemes began as a simple reward for loyal passengers. Over time, however, airlines discovered that selling points to banks and credit-card companies was more profitable than flying some of their routes. ---- For some airlines, the loyalty programme is now worth more than the planes themselves.

options.o1: The banks give these points to their own customers as an incentive to spend more.
options.o2: Passengers who fly most often still receive the largest number of points.
options.o3: Some routes are flown at a loss because they are politically important.
options.o4: Airport lounges are open only to members of the scheme.
options.o5: The first such scheme was introduced by an American airline in 1981.

questions.why: Önceki cümle puanların bankalara satıldığını, sonraki cümle programın uçaklardan değerli hâle geldiğini söyler; boşluk bankaların bu puanlarla ne yaptığını açıklayıp iki cümleyi bağlamalıdır. incentive 'teşvik' demektir.
questions.trap_note: Doğru bir bilgidir ama programın ilk hâline geri döner; bankalarla kurulan yeni ilişkiyi açıklamadığı için akışı keser.

questions.subject: social custom / wedding gift lists
questions.stem: Wedding gift lists were once considered rather rude, because they told guests exactly what to buy. Today they are common, and most guests say that they prefer them. The reason is simple. A list removes the risk of buying something that the couple already owns or will never use. ----

options.o1: What once seemed to restrict the guests' choice is now valued for sparing them a difficult decision.
options.o2: For this reason, most couples now ask their guests not to bring any gifts at all.
options.o3: Wedding ceremonies have become considerably more expensive in recent decades.
options.o4: Some shops charge the couple a small fee for managing the list.
options.o5: Many couples are now choosing to get married abroad.

questions.why: Boşluk paragrafın son cümlesidir: baştaki 'kaba sayılırdı' ile ortadaki 'tercih ediliyor' arasındaki değişimi tek cümlede bağlamalıdır.
questions.trap_note: 'For this reason' ile sonuç gibi görünür ama paragrafın anlattığı listeyi değil, hediyesizliği savunur.

questions.subject: media / podcast advertising
questions.stem: In many podcasts, the host reads the adverts personally instead of playing a recorded message. ---- Listeners who would skip a normal advert often keep listening, because the voice belongs to someone they have chosen to spend an hour with every week. Advertisers pay extra for this, and some hosts now turn down sponsors whose products they would not use themselves.

options.o1: This makes the advert feel like a recommendation from someone the listener trusts.
options.o2: This makes the advert shorter and cheaper to produce than a recorded one.
options.o3: Podcasts have become popular among commuters who travel by train.
options.o4: Recorded adverts were common on radio for most of the last century.
options.o5: Some podcasts are produced by large media companies with their own studios.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonraki cümle dinleyicinin neden reklamı atlamadığını açıklar: ses güvendiği birine aittir. Boşluk bu güveni adlandırmalıdır.
questions.trap_note: 'This makes the advert' kalıbıyla doğru şıkla aynı başlar, ama maliyetten söz ettiği için sonraki cümledeki dinleyici davranışını açıklamaz.

questions.subject: higher education / textbook prices
sentences: University textbooks have become far more expensive over the last two decades, even though printing has become cheaper.
The main reason is that the person who chooses the book is not the person who pays for it.
A lecturer selects the text for a course, and students have little choice but to buy it at whatever price the publisher sets.
Many students prefer printed textbooks to digital ones because they find it easier to concentrate on paper.
Economists describe this as a market in which the usual pressure to lower prices does not prevail.
questions.why: IV. cümle de ders kitabından söz eder ama konuyu fiyattan basılı-dijital tercihine kaydırır; paragrafın 'seçen ile ödeyen farklı kişi' zincirini koparır.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle bir yorum gibi durur ama paragrafın bütün açıklamasını başlatan nedendir; III ve V ona dayanır.

questions.subject: food waste / community fridges
sentences: Community fridges allow shops and residents to leave surplus food in a public place where anyone can take it.
Some shops worry that giving food away might reduce their sales of the same products.
Organisers expected the fridges to be used mainly by people on low incomes.
In practice, the users include students, office workers and pensioners, and the organisers see this as a strength.
Because nobody has to prove that they are poor, people feel no embarrassment about taking food that would otherwise be thrown away.
questions.why: II. cümle mağazalar ve yiyecek sözcükleriyle konuya bağlı görünür, ama dükkânların satış kaygısına geçer ve bu konu bir daha açılmaz; akış 'kimin kullandığı' sorusu üzerinden ilerler.
questions.trap_note: IV. cümle beklenmedik bir bilgi verdiği için sapma sanılır; oysa III'teki beklentiyi düzelten ve V'i hazırlayan halkadır.

questions.subject: economics / local currencies
sentences: Some towns have introduced their own local currencies, which can be spent only in shops within the area.
The aim is to keep money circulating in the local economy instead of flowing out to large national chains.
Many European countries have replaced their national currencies with the euro over the last thirty years.
Studies suggest that the economic effect is modest, because most residents still do the bulk of their shopping in ordinary money.
Supporters argue that the real benefit is not economic at all but a stronger sense of belonging to the town.
questions.why: III. cümle 'currency' sözcüğünü paylaşır ama yerel paradan ulusal para birliğine geçer; paragrafın yerel ekonomi zincirini koparır.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle ekonomiden uzaklaştığı için sapma sanılır; oysa IV'teki 'etki sınırlı' saptamasına destekçilerin verdiği yanıttır.

questions.subject: democracy / citizens' assemblies
sentences: A citizens' assembly brings together a randomly selected group of ordinary people to study a difficult political question.
Members hear evidence from experts, discuss it in small groups and then vote on a set of recommendations.
Because the members are not elected, they have no reason to worry about losing their seats at the next election.
Elections in most democracies are held every four or five years, and turnout has fallen in many of them.
This freedom often allows them to endorse compromises that professional politicians would be afraid to support.
questions.why: IV. cümle 'election' sözcüğünü paylaşır ama seçimlerin sıklığına ve katılım oranına geçer; III'teki özgürlük ile V'teki uzlaşma arasındaki bağı koparır.
questions.trap_note: III. cümle de seçimden söz ettiği için sapma sanılır; oysa V'teki 'This freedom' ifadesinin gösterdiği özgürlük odur.

questions.subject: everyday technology / weather apps
sentences: A weather app that shows a seventy per cent chance of rain is not saying that it will rain for seventy per cent of the day.
It means that, on days with similar conditions in the past, rain fell somewhere in the area on about seven days out of ten.
Many users misread the figure, and some conclude that the forecast was wrong whenever the day stays dry.
Forecasters have tried showing the same information as a simple picture, which most people find easier to understand.
Weather apps are among the applications that people download most often to their phones.
questions.why: V. cümle hava durumu uygulamalarından söz eder ama uygulamanın popülerliğine geçer; paragrafın konusu yüzde değerinin nasıl okunması gerektiğidir.
questions.trap_note: I. cümle olumsuz bir tanımla başladığı için sapma sanılır; oysa paragrafın düzelttiği yanlış okumayı ilk kez dile getiren cümledir.
